body:
Interesting, thanks for the report!

@stuartwdouglas , @geoand could one of you have a look or suggest someone to assign to?

Note in this particular project, hbm.xml files are being used, which means we record POJOs representing the content of those XML files during the build. This may or may not be the reason for the class file being "too large".

(One of the goals being to avoid XML parsing when the application starts, we cannot simply read the XML files again during static init).

Stuart had solved a similar issue for generated methods that were too large by breaking them up. 
However the problem here is that the constant pool of the to be generated class is too large (it does not have to do with the fact that the application uses XML), which I don't know how we can solve since each recorder step is associated with a single generated class

On Further Analysis found that Constant Pool Count is `253878` which is more than `65535` hence asm ClassWriter is throwing exception.
I could not reproduce this even with 4k entities. What is filling up the const pool in this case?
https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/22932 may help here, but I need to make some recorder improvements to fix this properly.

issue.title: Reduce amount of bytecode generated
issue.body:
Reduces the amount of code generated by the bytecode recorders. In
particular:

- Don't store values in the cross-method array unless they are actually
  used be a later method
- Add objects to collections earlier to reduce the chance the add code
  will be in a different method to the load code

Fixes #22833
